title: Hercules and his 12 labors
subtitle: From chaos to Olympus
subject: mythologie
description: Heracles, son of Zeus, kills his own family in a fit of madness. His Twelve Labors are a penance: kill monsters, then defeat death itself.

hero.hook: Twelve trials to wash away one crime. A half god who ends up among the gods.

blocks.text: **Heracles**, called **Hercules** by the Romans, is the greatest Greek hero. Son of [[Zeus]], king of the gods, and of the mortal woman **Alcmene**, he is far more than a strongman. He stands for force, but also for violence and redemption.

His **Twelve Labors** are not a freely chosen quest for glory. They are a penance for a terrible crime. By clearing the world of monsters, Heracles opened the road to civilization, and won a rare privilege: immortality.

sections.title: Hera's madness, the crime, the penance

blocks.text: [[Hera]], the lawful wife of Zeus, hated the child born of his infidelity. She sent two snakes to the cradle. The baby strangled them with his bare hands. Later Heracles married **Megara**, daughter of the king of Thebes. Hera then struck him with madness, and he slaughtered his wife and children.

That blood crime, a [[Miasma]], placed him outside human society. The oracle of Delphi ordered him to serve his cousin, King **Eurystheus**. This fearful ruler, guided by Hera, set him ten labors, then twelve, because he refused to count some of them.
Legend says that Hera's milk, spurting from her breast while she was tricked into nursing Heracles, formed the **Milky Way** across the sky.

The first challenge was the **Nemean Lion**, whose hide no weapon could pierce. Heracles strangled it, then skinned it with its own claws. That skin, the [[Leonte]], became his armor. Next came the **Lernaean Hydra**, a serpent with many heads: for every head cut off, two grew back. With his nephew Iolaus, he burned the necks shut with fire.

blocks.caption: Heracles against the Nemean Lion and the Hydra

blocks.text: The ancients said Zeus had set the Nemean Lion among the stars: the constellation **Leo**.

The **Augean Stables** changed the register. Thousands of cattle had lived there for thirty years without the place ever being cleaned. Eurystheus wanted to humiliate the hero. Heracles diverted two rivers, the [[Alpheus]] and the Peneus, and in a single day the current carried the dung away. Intelligence counted as much as muscle.

sections.title: To the ends of the world

blocks.text: The labors took him far from Greece: the Cretan Bull, the man eating mares, the belt of **Hippolyta**, queen of the Amazons. To reach the cattle of the giant **Geryon**, in the far West, Heracles opened a passage between the Mediterranean and the Atlantic: the [[Pillars of Hercules]], today the Strait of Gibraltar.

He stole the **golden apples** of the Hesperides by outwitting the Titan [[Atlas]], who carries the sky on his shoulders. The last labor was the worst: go down to the Underworld and bring back **Cerberus**, the dog with many heads. To come out alive was, symbolically, to defeat death.
The explorer Orellana is said to have named the **Amazon** river after thinking he saw women warriors on its banks, an echo of the Amazons of myth.

sections.title: Apotheosis: a hero becomes a god

blocks.text: The Labors ended, but the tragedies did not. His wife **Deianira** gave him a tunic soaked in the poisoned blood of the [[centaur]] Nessus. Burning alive, Heracles climbed onto a pyre on Mount Oeta. His mortal part burned away. His divine essence rose to Olympus: this is the **apotheosis**.

blocks.caption: The apotheosis of Heracles: the hero joins the gods

blocks.text: Reconciled with Hera, he married **Hebe**, eternal youth. The Romans took up his figure under the name **Hercules**. A “herculean task” still means an enormous job. Heracles is not only a killer of monsters: he is an architect of order.
**Heracles** (Hercules) performed twelve labors to atone for the murder of his family. From the Nemean Lion to Cerberus, he moved from chaos to civilization, and won immortality.
